test_command: dotnet build api/Biolog.Api/Biolog.Api.csproj && dotnet test tests/features/bio-idn-001/Biolog.Features.PersonRegistry.Tests.csproj && dotnet test tests/dotnet/Biolog.IntegrationTests/Biolog.IntegrationTests.csproj && dotnet test tests/dotnet/Biolog.UnitTests/Biolog.UnitTests.csproj && bash scripts/quality.sh
summary: Closes Seyi's round-1 QA-01 High finding: IPersonRepository.CreateAsync/ReplaceAsync and the concrete repository were public, and Person used a public object initializer with no declared constructor, so an independent probe could construct a Person directly and call the repository to move it to a foreign tenant and jump it straight to ARCHIVED, bypassing PersonService entirely (no lock, no lifecycle check, no audit event). Fixed in three layers: (1) Person's constructor is now internal with Id/TenantId as get-only (no init) - immutable even across a `with` expression, mirroring BIO-TEN-002-QA-03's TenantContext fix exactly; (2) IPersonRepository/InMemoryPersonRepository are now internal, reachable only from this assembly, Biolog.Api (DI registration) and the test project (an explicit InternalsVisibleTo seam); (3) the repository independently re-validates identity/tenant immutability and lifecycle legality at the persistence boundary via a new shared Domain/PersonLifecycleTransitions.cs (extracted so PersonService and the repository check the identical rule, not two copies that could drift) - the same dual-boundary discipline CredentialReferenceValidator (BIO-DEV-001-QA-04) established. New tests/features/bio-idn-001/PersonRepositoryGovernanceTests.cs (9 tests) drives every attack the review named directly against the repository, plus reflection tests proving the surface is inaccessible to ordinary production consumers and Person has no public constructor.
notes: Verified end-to-end: dotnet build api/Biolog.Api clean (0 warnings/errors) - confirms minimal-API endpoint parameter binding and DI registration both work fine with the now-internal PersonService/IPersonRepository types through the real packaged host, not just at the feature-project level. 70/70 feature-local tests (61 pre-existing + 9 new governance tests). 154/154 dotnet unit tests (unaffected). 54/54 dotnet integration tests (unaffected, including all 5 PersonHostChannelTests still passing through WebApplicationFactory<Program> - proves the internal-visibility change did not break the real shipped-host tenant-resolution path). 47/47 offline structural checks (9 new QA-01-specific checks, one existing check updated to reference the transition table's new shared location). dotnet vulnerability audit clean. contract-freeze PASS. traceability PASS. module-project-reference-direction PASS. Full scripts/quality.sh (repo-wide gate): QUALITY: PASS, 0 failures.
